bull.b: A sizable equity base with very low debt and cash plus marketable securities north of $240M provides multi-quarter runway. This capital cushion reduces immediate financing risk, lets management prioritize product and utilization fixes, and supports investment in higher-margin channels while scaling.

Half the company's revenue now comes from recurring streams (software, fleet services, advertising), pointing to more predictable cash flows over time. A rising software and ad mix supports better margins long-term and reduces sensitivity to single large delivery partners as core delivery monetization matures.

A national fleet of ~2,000 robots and the Diligent Robotics acquisition create scale advantages for route density, ad inventory, and recurring hospital contracts. Scale and specialized indoor robotics diversify use cases, improving unit economics potential and widening addressable markets beyond sidewalk delivery.

bear.b: Steep gross losses indicate current unit economics do not cover direct operating costs. Unless per-delivery costs fall or higher-margin software/ads scale materially, structural unprofitability will persist, forcing sustained subsidy or price increases that could hinder adoption and long-term margin sustainability.

bear.t: High cash burn and operating losses
bear.b: Consistent multi-hundred-million dollar cash outflows require continued funding or rapid margin improvement. Even with a healthy cash balance today, prolonged negative operating and free cash flow pressures strategic freedom, increases dilution risk, and constrains ability to invest aggressively in commercialization or R&D long-term.

A material guidance reset driven by loss of expected Uber volume highlights partner concentration and integration risk. Reliance on large platform partners for utilization exposes revenue to single-counterparty changes, forcing costly fleet reallocation and creating durable uncertainty until new high-utilization channels are secured.
